Nodes.Text: "Yes. I was." {n}She does not argue it.{/n} "That is the most dangerous sentence a mortal has ever said to me, and it is true, and I am going to write it down so that I never believe it again."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text: "I did not see it. I suspected, at the end. I did not see it." {n}She looks at the turned chair.{/n} "He brought me the idea of a Council. He brought me you. He waited at my table for someone who never came, and I thought, all that while, that he was debating."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: "You set it, Madam Chair. He only suggested it."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Eritrice

Choices.Text: "You weren't wasted. You were the only one of them who meant it."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Eritrice

Choices.Text: "I don't know. That's the honest answer. I don't know."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text: "Did you believe him?"

Choices.Text: "No. But he deserved a crown more than most kings I've met."
"I trusted my intuition. It said: it's all true."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"That is not a reason to crown a man. That is a reason to buy him a drink." {n}But the tip of her quill taps the table, once, which in her is almost a laugh.{/n}
"He fought off demons afterwards, I am told. With a tankard, and his friends, and a great deal of singing. The reports are not clear, because the men who wrote them were also drunk." {n}She sighs.{/n} "I cannot refute it. I have tried. I have minuted it as 'unverified, regrettably plausible'."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Your intuition." {n}The growl is very soft.{/n} "I have spent my existence arguing that truth is found through honest debate. You found it by feeling it in a tavern and saying it out loud until it was so." {n}Her claws curl.{/n}
"That is not how it works. That cannot be how it works. If it is how it works, then my Council is a very elaborate way of doing slowly what you do in an evening with a crown and a pig."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
{n}Her whiskers settle, slowly.{/n} "That is the correct answer. It is the only answer that does not terrify me." {n}She writes it down.{/n}
"If you had said 'before', I would have had to believe that you found a buried truth, which is what I do. If you had said 'after', I would have had to believe that you make them, which is what I fear. 'I do not know' leaves room for both. You have taught me to leave room for both."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: "Because you're the one thing I can't make true by saying it."
"Because it only works on fools and kings. You're neither."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
{n}She stares at you. Then something in her face gives, like a knot coming loose.{/n}
"Yes. That is right. You cannot say 'the chair agrees' and make it so. You have to argue. You have to win the vote." {n}She takes up the quill.{/n} "That is why you come here. It is the only table in your life where your tricks do not work. I have been flattering myself that it was my conversation."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Thaberdine is king of Sarkoris, then. Or of a tavern. The record will show whichever proves true, when it proves true." {n}She writes, in the upright hand:{/n} "The Commander crowned a king. The chair reserves judgement on the king. The chair has formed her judgement on the Commander, and declines to minute it."
{n}Without looking up, she adds:{/n} "It is not unfavourable. That is all you are getting."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: "I have dealings with her. They're not the Council's business."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"No, you were not. Socothbenoth was looking at the door. You were looking at it with him." {n}She does not raise her voice.{/n}
"You may keep your dealings from me. You may not tell me they do not exist. Rule two." {n}She waits.{/n}

Choices.Text: "...I have dealings with her. They're not the Council's business."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text: "It is my element. I cannot stop noticing any more than you can stop playing tricks." {n}A pause.{/n} "And I notice that you have not denied anything."

Choices.Text: "I have dealings with her. They're not the Council's business."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: "Would it bother you? If it were more than dealings?"
"You'd really sit at a table with her?"

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Yes." {n}Immediately, and then, carefully:{/n} "It would bother the lion. The chair would note that the Commander keeps company with a demon lord who has never told the truth in her existence, and that the Commander keeps company with the chair, who has never told anything else. The chair would find that very interesting, and would want to understand it."
{n}The fur along her jaw rises and settles.{/n} "Understanding things is how I stop them from bothering me. It has never failed yet. I suspect Nocticula will be the first."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"I sit at a table with her brother. I sat at one with Alichino for a very long time before I noticed what he was." {n}She considers.{/n}
"I would sit at a table with Nocticula, yes, if she would sit and argue instead of seducing the chairs. I doubt she would. But the offer would be minuted. Every plane is welcome at my table. That was always the point, and I will not make an exception because the Commander looks at doors."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"The chair's ruling." {n}She writes as she speaks.{/n} "The Commander's dealings with the Lady in Shadow are not the Council's business. The chair notes that they exist. The chair does not object. The chair will growl."
{n}She sands the line.{/n} "There. It is true, and it is fair, and it is minuted. You may go and look at doors."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: "Keep it. You'll remember it better than I will."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"That is true. It is not the point." {n}She presses it into your hands, and this time lets go.{/n}
"The minutes are not for the one who keeps them. They are for the one who needs to know, later, what was really said. That is you, Commander. On some bad night at the edge of the Worldwound, you will need to know that someone argued with you as an equal and lost, gladly, and wrote it down."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
{n}It is heavier than it looks. She watches you hold it with an expression you have seen on her only when a vote is being counted.{/n}
"Read the first line. Not now. When I am not watching. I could not bear to watch you read it."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: [Unroll it to the end, in front of her.]

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Later." {n}She nods, too quickly.{/n} "Yes. That is better. When I am not here." {n}She busies herself with the Council's scroll, and her hand is not steady.{/n}
"If you are ever in doubt of anything, Commander, read it. I have never written anything that was not true. I have never written anything truer than that."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Carried." {n}Her voice is not quite steady.{/n}
"The chair has now said it. In writing. Which counts. It is minuted in two places now, and you are holding one of them." {n}She reaches over and rolls the scroll closed in your hands, gently, and ties the ribbon.{/n} "Take care of it. It is the only fair copy. I could make another. I will not."

Scenes.Title: A motion to expel
Scenes.Entry: "You look like you've had a letter from Hell."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"From Erebus. Alichino does not attend sessions, but he writes." {n}She lays the letter on the table between you, face up. The hand is small and very neat, and the seal is black.{/n}
"He moves that the mortal member be expelled from the Council. The grounds are that the Commander 'brings the petty concerns of a single crusade to a body concerned with the multiverse', that the Commander 'is unreliable in procedure', and that the Commander 'adjourns meetings without the authority of the chair'." {n}She pauses.{/n} "The last is true." {n}She turns the page.{/n} "He supports the second ground by quoting, in full, the chair's own censure of you, for the motion you carried in a room with no floor. He has copied it out of my minutes in a very small, very neat hand. I told you he would."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text: "He said, the day you met him, that he would remember your audacity. He does. Devils always do. It is the most reliable thing about them." {n}Her claws tap the black seal, once.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: [Trickster] "Let me handle Alichino. By the next session, he'll withdraw it himself."
"Put it on the agenda. I'll argue my own case."
"Recuse yourself. You can't chair a vote on me."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"I do not want to know how." {n}At once.{/n} "If you tell me how, I will have to minute it, and if it is what I suspect, I will have to minute it with a very specific word."
{n}She weighs you, the way she weighs an amendment.{/n} "If Alichino withdraws his own motion, freely, in writing, the chair will accept the withdrawal. The chair will not inquire into his reasons. The chair notes that she has never before declined to inquire into anything." {n}She looks, for a moment, almost smug.{/n} "Go. Before I change my mind."

Choices.Text: [Go and find a devil's weak spot.]

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Eritrice
Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
{n}As you turn to go:{/n} "Whatever happens at that session, it will be minuted truly. If they expel you, I will write it down. And then I will write a dissent, in my own name, as the chair, which I have never done." {n}She looks at the black seal.{/n}
"It will be very long. It will be the best thing I have ever written. Alichino will have to read all of it, because the rules require it."

Choices.Text: [Leave her drafting the dissent in advance.]

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice

Choices.Text: "Rule one: everyone keeps their own minutes."
"Rule one: nobody may carry a weapon into the hall. Not even the chair."
"Rule one: any member may move a motion from the floor. Even a mortal."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Everyone keeps their own minutes." {n}She turns the idea over.{/n} "So that nobody can claim the record was falsified, because there are a hundred records, and they must all be reconciled. It would take forever."
{n}Her whiskers lift.{/n} "It would take forever. It would also make lying at the Crossroads almost impossible, because a hundred planes would have to tell the same lie." {n}She writes it at the top of a fresh scroll.{/n} "Rule one. Carried. Next."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Eritrice
Eritrice

Choices.Text: "It should be you. Not because you dreamed it. Because you're the only one who'd let it outvote you."
"Rotate it. Every plane chairs in turn. Even the Abyss."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
"Even the Abyss." {n}She winces, visibly.{/n} "A demon lord chairing a session of the Crossroads. Deskari's heralds calling the planes to order."
"...It is correct. If the forum means what it says, every plane must be able to hold the chair, and every plane must be able to lose it. Otherwise it is only my Council with a larger table." {n}She writes it.{/n} "I will be the first chair. You will allow me that. Then I will hand it on. And I will keep the minutes of whoever follows, because somebody must."

Nodes.Speaker: Eritrice
Nodes.Text:
{n}You work on the standing orders until the lamp needs trimming, and then past it. She writes; you argue; she strikes out; you laugh; she growls and writes it anyway. At the end there are nine rules on a clean scroll, and at the foot of it she has left a space for two signatures.{/n}
"The war is not won. The Worldwound is not a crossroads. Nothing on this scroll is true yet." {n}She signs.{/n} "But it is written down, in two hands, and I have never yet abandoned a thing I wrote down in my own. Sign, Commander."

Scenes.Title: The subject's file
Scenes.Entry: [Ask for your file] "Detailed notes, from before I was born. I'm the subject. I'd like a copy."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}Areelu's face does something it has not done since the mirror: something she did not plan. One eyebrow rises a fraction, and stays there.{/n}
"A copy." {n}She repeats it the way a physician repeats a symptom.{/n} "Subjects do not read their files. It contaminates the results. A rat that has read its own maze is no longer a rat, and it is no longer a maze."

Choices.Text: "Then I'm contaminated already. I found your laboratory, your mirror and your dretch. What else is in the file?"
[Joke] "If I'm your creation, every joke I make is technically yours. Congratulations. You're funnier than you look."
[Joke] "I'll trade you. I've been keeping notes on you too. Mine are shorter."
"Never mind. Tell me what I came to hear."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Everything." {n}Her gaze does not leave you.{/n} "The first fever. The first lie you told that was believed. The crevice in Kenabres, where I saved you and your unfortunate companions, and you never knew who to thank."
"And a gap. Some while ago the notes stopped agreeing with you. You began to do things I had not written down. That is not your triumph, Commander. It is my error, and I have been correcting errors since before your grandparents were born."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text: "You keep notes on me." {n}It is not quite a question. She tilts the mirror toward you as if it might show her the page.{/n} "Read me the first entry."

Choices.Text: "'Arrived uninvited before I was born. Stayed. Still hasn't explained herself.'"
"'Turned herself into half a demon to win an argument with the gods. Still losing.'"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Accurate, and useless. You have described the phenomenon without measuring it." {n}A thin, cold smile.{/n}
"That is the difference between us, Commander. You notice. I measure. One day that difference will decide which of us walks out of Threshold."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"No. You may not have a copy." {n}She lifts the mirror, considers her own reflection in it, and lowers it again.{/n}
"But I will give you something rarer than my notes. An entry of your own." {n}She speaks as if dictating to someone who is not in the room.{/n} "'In Alushinyrra, the subject asked to read the file. Unprecedented. Further observation required.'"

Choices.Text: "Further observation. I'll hold you to that."
"If your notes are so good, predict what I'll say next."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Very well." {n}She does not even pause to think.{/n} "You will say something clever about my mirror. When I do not laugh, you will say something rude about my dretch. When he laughs and I do not, you will ask me a real question, because that is what you do when a joke fails: you reach for the truth, as a drunk reaches for a wall."
{n}She folds her hands.{/n} "Go on. Prove me wrong."

Choices.Text: "Why me? Out of everyone in Golarion, why did you choose me?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}The silence stretches. The Suture fidgets. Somewhere in the palace a gong is struck, and dies away.{/n}
"Silence." {n}Her eyes narrow very slightly, and you have the distinct impression that she has stopped reading you off a page and started looking.{/n} "That was not in the file either. You are becoming expensive to study, Commander."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I did not write it down." {n}For the space of a heartbeat something that is almost amusement moves behind her eyes. Then it is put away, like an instrument into its case.{/n}
"I will not need to. I do not forget variables that make jokes at my expense." "Ask your questions, Commander. You have spent a part of your answers on me."

Scenes.Title: My money's on neither
Scenes.Entry: [Offer the Architect a bet] "One of us has to die so the other can live and the Wound can close. I'll take that bet. My money's on 'neither'."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: "Debts get paid by whoever can't get out of them. I always get out of them."
"You don't sound certain. You sound like someone who checked her sums twice."
"You said you'd need further observation. Here I am. Observe."
[Joke] "Then I'll owe you. I'm very good at owing."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Everyone who has ever owed me something said the same. Most of them are in the Wound now." {n}She does not raise her voice. She has never needed to.{/n}
"But I will allow that you have been difficult to collect." {n}She gestures, very slightly, at the dead city around you.{/n} "Iz owed me once, too. Look how thoroughly it paid."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"You are being observed. You are also standing in a trap that Deskari built for you, which rather spoils the experiment." {n}Her mouth thins.{/n}
"In Alushinyrra you asked for your file. Now you offer me a wager. You are acquiring habits, Commander. Habits can be predicted."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Very well. I accept that you have made an offer. I do not accept its terms." {n}She glances past you: toward the camp, the burning temple, the city folding in on itself like wet paper.{/n}
"State your stake when you know what you can afford to lose. You will not learn it here. Here, you are about to lose a great deal."

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Among the loot from Iz is a lens of dark glass in a silver ring, cold to the touch. Nobody remembers picking it up.{/n}
{n}When you hold it to your eye you do not see the tent around you. You see your tent from above, as a bird would, and a woman's hand at a desk, writing notes about it. The hand is steady. The margins are full of small, neat corrections.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Tap the lens twice] "Knock knock. You've been watching me since Kenabres. Rude not to say hello."
[Hold the lens up to the lamp and read her notes backwards.]
[Wrap it in cloth and put it away.]

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Held to the lamp, the notes read backwards through the glass. Most of them are about you: your hours, your rations, which of your companions you laugh with and which you only answer. At the bottom, underlined twice: "Subject remains unpredictable. Correction scheduled for Threshold."{/n}
{n}The hand stops writing. Then, very deliberately, it adds: "Subject is reading this."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Breathe on the glass and write in the mist] "Correction? I prefer 'punchline'."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: "Then measure this. One of us is supposed to burn at the end. My money's on neither."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: "Then here's a line you didn't write. One of us is supposed to burn. My money's on neither."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: [Keep the lens, and put it away.]
"Why would you give your enemy a window into your study?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I did not give it to you. You picked it up out of the ruins of Iz, where I dropped it while I was warning you about Deskari's trap, which you did not thank me for either."
{n}A pause.{/n} "And a window works both ways, Commander. Every time you look through it, you tell me something: when you are awake, when you are alone, how long you can bear to look at me before you put me away. I have learned more about you from how you hold this glass than from a year of notes."

Choices.Text: [Keep the lens, and put it away.]

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator

"Because I've already died once. It didn't take."

"In Kenabres, in the crevice, twice. In Drezen, once, very nearly. You do not stay dead, Commander. That is not courage. It is a property, like the boiling point of water, and I would very much like to know who set it."

Nodes.Text:
"Nobody has read how it ends. I have been writing it for a century, and even I have not read it."
{n}The frost hesitates.{/n} "And yet you say it as if it were true. That is what makes you difficult, Commander. When you lie, the world leans closer to listen."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"You do not. I have seen you hide things. You hide them badly and cheerfully, like a child with a stolen cake behind its back."
{n}A pause, long enough that the frost begins to melt at the edges.{/n} "I did not say that to be cruel. I said it because it is accurate. I have seen a great many children hiding things."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}The frost goes blank. For a long time nothing forms in it at all.{/n}
"That is not an answer. That is a provocation. I will record it as one." {n}Then, smaller, in the corner of the glass:{/n} "Recorded."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text: "Second. What is a soul, to a Trickster? The priests say it is a thing to be weighed. The demons say it is a thing to be eaten. I have spent a hundred years treating it as a thing to be mended, and I have not managed it. What do you say it is?"

Choices.Text: "A joke the gods haven't finished telling."
"Something that belongs to whoever it's in."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Whoever it is in." {n}The frost cracks, very faintly, along one edge of the glass.{/n}
"You do not know what you have said. You will, at Threshold. Remember that you said it, Commander. I will."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Paperwork." {n}A long pause.{/n} "The Lady of Graves keeps it, and she has never once lost a page. I know. I have looked for the one I wanted."
"Do not joke about that particular ledger. Not to me. Not yet."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}The frost clears. Nothing forms in it; the lamp gutters twice. Then:{/n}
"Third. When you look at me through this glass, Commander, what do you see? Be precise. I will know if you are being kind."

Choices.Text: "A woman who hasn't slept in a hundred years."
"The only person who's ever taken notes on me."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"The only one who has taken notes on you. Yes." {n}Something in the writing changes: the letters are no less precise, but they lean, very slightly, as if the hand were tired.{/n}
"Everyone else looks at you and sees a saviour, or a monster, or a clown. I look at you and see a record. It is the most intimate thing I know how to do. Do not make me regret telling you so."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Frost." {n}The glass fogs over completely, and clears, and fogs again: once, twice, three times.{/n}
"That was a laugh, Commander. I thought you should know what one looks like, from this side. Do not expect another."

Nodes.Text:
{n}The frost fades, and before she can clear the glass again it is you who breathes on it, and writes in the mist with a fingertip: "Where were you, all those years you were watching?"{/n}
{n}The answer is a long time coming. When it comes, the letters fill the whole lens, edge to edge, and she has to clear it twice to finish.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Put the lens away for the night.]

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Where you needed me, which was nearly everywhere. In Kenabres, when you fell into the crevice with your unfortunate companions, I saved you. At the Gray Garrison I distracted Minagho, so you could reach the wardstone. In Drezen I wore Yaniel's face to guide you to the Sword of Valor."
"I told you all of this in Alushinyrra. You did not thank me then. Do not thank me now."

Choices.Text: [Joke] "Thank you. You were a terrible Yaniel, by the way."
"You kept me alive so you could kill me at Threshold."
"And in Drezen, lately? Were you watching when I crowned the Fool King?"
"What's the last thing you watched me do, before I asked?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I was an excellent Yaniel. You followed her, did you not? You went exactly where she led you. That is the only measure of a disguise that matters."
{n}The frost settles.{/n} "It was the first time I spoke to you with a face. I chose a kind one. You did not notice the difference. Neither, I confess, did I, until afterwards."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Because you asked where I was, and it is a question nobody has asked me for a hundred years. They ask what I did. They ask how many. Never where I was."
{n}The frost thins.{/n} "I was at a great many windows, Commander. Most of them were yours."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Yes." {n}No hesitation at all.{/n} "I kept you alive so that you would be whole when it mattered. A vessel that breaks too early is useless."
"You wanted me to say something softer. I do not have anything softer. I have this, which is true, and which I have never said to anyone else."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The night after Iz, among the loot your people carried out of the ruins, there is a lens of dark glass in a silver ring. It is cold to the touch, and it is lying on your camp table, on top of your maps, exactly where you would put your hand.{/n}
{n}Nobody admits to having put it there. Nobody, when you ask, remembers seeing it at all.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}You turn the lens face down on the table. After a moment the silver ring grows cold enough to frost the wood around it, and letters form in the frost, reversed, so that you have to read them in your shaving mirror:{/n}
"Face down. As if that has ever stopped me. You offered me a wager at Iz, Commander. Pick me up."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}Through the glass you see your own tent from above, as a bird would see it, and a woman's hand at a desk, writing. The hand pauses. Frost creeps across the lens from the other side, and letters form in it.{/n}
"You offered me a wager at Iz. I am told gamblers like to watch their opponents' faces. Here is mine. Try not to waste it."

Choices.Text: [Joke] "Your handwriting is terrible. Is that the Abyss, or just you?"
[Breathe on the glass and write] "Show me your face."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}The frost clears completely. For one long moment the glass shows you nothing but a desk, a lamp, and the edge of a sleeve. Then the sleeve moves, and the lamp is turned, deliberately, so that the light falls away from whoever is sitting there.{/n}
"No." {n}The letters form slowly this time.{/n} "You have seen my face at Iz, and in Alushinyrra, and you will see it again at Threshold. Here you may have my hand. It is the part of me that has done the most damage. It seems fair that it is the part you should watch."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"It is Sarkorian, and it was thought very fine, once, by people who are now in the Wound." {n}The frost thickens with something that might be irritation.{/n}
"You are the only living creature who has ever mocked my hand. Most people are too busy being frightened of what it wrote."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I did knock. At Kenabres, at Drezen, in Alushinyrra. You were always too busy being alive to answer."
{n}The frost clears, and forms again.{/n} "Keep the lens. I will watch you through it, as I always have. You may watch me through it, if you can bear to. We will see which of us learns more before Threshold."

Scenes.Title: Whoever burns pays up
Scenes.Entry: "One of us must burn. About that: I have a bet for you."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"A bet." {n}The projection folds its arms. In the light of the device she looks carved out of smoke, all but the wound above her heart, which is very red.{/n}
"You have been saving it, I think. Well? Put it on the table. Mine is the only table left in the Abyss that you have not overturned."

Choices.Text: "You heard it at Iz. One of us burns, you say. I say neither."
"You read it in the frost. One of us burns, you say. I say neither."
"You asked me three questions through the frost. Here's the answer to a fourth: neither of us burns."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Neither." {n}She tastes the word the way she tasted it at Iz, and likes it no better.{/n}
"I have had since Iz to consider it. It is not a wager, Commander. It is a joke with the stake missing. I do not accept jokes as collateral."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Neither." {n}Her voice is dry.{/n} "You made your offer through my own lens, late, when you might have made it to my face at Iz. I dislike being approached through the back door of my instruments."
"But I read what I write, and what you wrote was not a joke. That is worse. I do not accept jokes as collateral, and I am not sure what else you have."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: [Name your stake] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."
[Refuse the Betrayer's bet] "I don't gamble with the woman who opened the Wound."
"Don't you want to know why I'd bet with you at all?"
"You asked me what I felt at the crib. Ask me what I feel now."
"You asked me what I felt at the crib. Ask me what I feel now."
"You asked me what I felt at the crib. Ask me what I feel now."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"No." {n}The answer comes too quickly, and she hears it come too quickly, and her mouth tightens.{/n}
"Yes. Very well. Yes. Everyone else who has stood in this cell came to kill me, or to beg me, or to ask me why. You came to gamble. I would like to know what you think you can win from a woman who has already lost everything that could be taken."

Choices.Text: "A reason to find out what you're like when you're not at war."
[Joke] "Your notes. I hear they're very thorough."

Nodes.Text:
"No." {n}The projection does not move.{/n} "You said sadness, at the crib. People offer me sadness as if it were a gift. It is only the mind admitting it cannot solve something."
"I did not stay sad, Commander. I stayed at the problem. Name your stake, or go."

Choices.Text: [Name your stake] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."
[Refuse the Betrayer's bet] "I don't gamble with the woman who opened the Wound."

Nodes.Text:
"No." {n}Something like approval flickers across her face and is gone.{/n} "You said rage, at the crib. That, at least, I recognise. It was the only honest thing the hunters ever taught me."
"But rage is a fuel, not a method. It burns out. Mine did, a long time ago, and I went on without it. Name your stake, or go."

Choices.Text: [Name your stake] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."
[Refuse the Betrayer's bet] "I don't gamble with the woman who opened the Wound."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"No." {n}She considers you with something dangerously close to interest.{/n} "You said closeness to mystery, at the crib. That is the answer I would once have given, before I learned that every mystery has a floor, and something waiting on it."
"You have not reached the floor yet. You will, at Threshold. Name your stake, or go."

Choices.Text: [Name your stake] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."
[Refuse the Betrayer's bet] "I don't gamble with the woman who opened the Wound."

Choices.Text: [Joke] "I'll shake when you're here in person. Bring the real hand to Threshold."
[Put your hand into the light where hers should be.]
[Joke] "Sure I know. Your notes. You're mostly paper by now."

Scenes.Title: The wager stands
Scenes.Entry: "Before I come in: the wager stands?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Stands?" {n}Areelu lowers her welcoming arms. The glow in her wound brightens and dims, like a slow breath.{/n}
"I have thought of little else, which annoys me. I made this prison into a laboratory, Commander, and the laboratory into a trap, and the trap into a door. And all the while, at the back of my mind, a voice saying: neither."

Choices.Text: "Sounds like you're losing sleep over me."
"Then you know I'm not coming in to lose."
"You said you'd keep my file until Threshold. Is it in there with you?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I have slept badly for a hundred years. You have not improved it." {n}The smile she gives you is thin, and very old.{/n}
"Be flattered, if it pleases you. It is the last pleasure you will be offered in this place."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Nobody comes to Threshold to lose. Everyone who ever came here meant to win: the hunters, the jailers, the knights of every crusade, and I."
{n}She glances up at the black walls, and her mouth is very nearly fond.{/n} "The prison kept all of us. It will keep whichever of us burns."
"I built my door out of its stones, Commander. Every wall you pass inside was once a wall that held me. Look at them as you go. I would like somebody, once, to look."

Scenes.Title: At the desk
Scenes.Entry: "You were at your desk, writing, when they came. You've been sitting at that desk ever since."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: "Then don't get up yet. Finish the entry. I'll wait."
"Threshold's hunters wanted a witch to burn. A hundred years on, they still haven't got one."
"In your cell you said you did it because you made a promise. That was the promise, wasn't it?"
"What were you writing? That night, at the desk."
[Joke] "Whatever you burn today, I hope it's the paperwork."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}Her laugh is short, and dreadful to hear.{/n} "They have wanted one since before your crusade had a name."
"Very well. If I burn today, I will burn as your wager, Commander, and not as their witch. It is a small distinction." {n}Her mouth tightens.{/n} "I find, to my irritation, that I prefer it."

Scenes.Title: What the winner keeps
Scenes.Entry: "Before we fight: if you win the wager, what will you do with my wound?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: [Joke] "That's the most romantic thing anyone's ever said to me."
"And if I win? What do I get?"
[Joke] "If I win, can I keep your notes? As a souvenir."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"A souvenir." {n}She says it as though tasting something she has never been offered before and does not trust.{/n}
"A century of the most dangerous research ever done on Golarion, bound in the skins of things you do not want to know about, and you would put it on a shelf beside a seashell." "No. If you win, my notes burn with me. Nobody will ever read them. That is not spite. It is the only kindness I know how to do the world."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Then you have been courted very badly." {n}Her lips thin, but something at the corner of her mouth refuses to obey her.{/n}
"A researcher must not have personal feelings for the subjects of her experiments. I said so. I have been saying so to myself since Iz."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Then I will have lost." {n}The wound above her heart pulses once, brightly.{/n}
"And I do not lose, Commander. I adjust the initial conditions, and I try again. But you ask as though you have already arranged it." {n}She studies your face.{/n} "Have you?"

Choices.Text: [Joke] "I never arrange anything. I just leave the door open and see who walks in."
"You said a researcher can't have feelings for her subjects. Do you?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu

Choices.Text: [Let her turn back to the rift.]

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Doors." {n}She glances at the rift behind her: the greatest open door in the world, which she made.{/n}
"Yes. I know something about doors, Commander. I know what walks in."

Choices.Text: [Let her turn back to the rift.]

Scenes.Title: The clause
Scenes.Entry: "Whatever you've hidden in this room, remember our terms. Whoever burns pays up. That includes burning yourself."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"The terms." {n}Areelu is swaying on her feet. Her hands will not keep still; she wrings them, and looks at them, and wrings them again.{/n}
"You would stand in the ruin of everything I built and quote my own wager at me, like a clerk reading a contract to a debtor."

Choices.Text: "If you burn by your own hand, you lose. In front of a witness."
"You'd rather die than let me win?"
[Joke] "I'd hate to win by forfeit. It's so undignified."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Undignified." {n}The word comes out of her like a cough.{/n} "You stand in my fortress, over my ruin, with my blood on your weapon, and you are worried about dignity."
"Very well. I will not hand you a forfeit. If I burn, you will have to earn it." {n}Her hands go still at last.{/n} "Remember that you asked for the hard way."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I would rather die than let anyone win. I have been doing it for a hundred years." {n}Her voice cracks on the last word, and she hates that it does.{/n}
"You are not special, Commander. You are merely the last."

Choices.Text: "Then you'd lose twice. Once to me, and once to the rules you wrote."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}She stops wringing her hands.{/n}
"You would hold me to that. Now. Here." {n}Something that is almost a laugh escapes her, and it hurts her to let it out.{/n} "It is a very good clause. I wrote it myself, and did not read it back."

Choices.Text: [Joke] "Read the small print. Burning yourself counts double."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}She looks at you with something very like hatred, and something else under it that she will not name.{/n}
"I will do exactly as I please with my own life, Commander. It is the only thing in this fortress that was ever mine." "But I will remember that you said it."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"There is no small print." {n}A pause.{/n} "...There is now. I can see it on your face."
{n}She closes her eyes. When she opens them the madness in them has banked, a little, like a fire someone has decided to keep until morning.{/n} "Very well. It is noted. Do not expect me to thank you for the footnote."

Scenes.Title: Terms, and worse
Scenes.Entry: "Before this ends, Areelu: I still have a bet for you."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"A bet, now? Here?" {n}She laughs, and it costs her. The wound above her heart bleeds afresh.{/n}
"You never came to my cell to make it. So the terms are mine, and they are worse. If you burn, I keep the wound. If I burn, you keep nothing: not my notes, not my name. Well?"

Choices.Text: [Take her terms] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"This is not a bargain. This is a woman bleeding on the floor of her own prison, offering you the last thing she owns at a terrible price." {n}She coughs, and there is blood in it.{/n}
"I have offered better terms to demon lords. They had the good manners to be on time." "Take it or leave it, Commander. I will not be asking twice."

Choices.Text: [Take her terms] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."

Choices.Text: [Take her terms] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."
"Your name? What would I do with your name?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: [Take her terms] "You stake what is left of you. I stake my wound. Whoever burns at Threshold pays up."

Scenes.Title: Into the cauldron
Scenes.Entry: [Take out the soul cauldron] "Time to collect the stake."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: "Will the rift take it in your place?"

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: [Collect the stake] "Whoever burns pays up. Pay into this."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}You set the cradle against the wound above her heart. For a moment nothing happens. Then the violet light comes out of her like blood from a cut: slowly, then all at once, pouring into the diamond until it glows like a small, furious star.{/n}
{n}She does not scream until the end. When it comes, it is the sound of something a century old being unstitched. The crimson goes out of her eyes. She stays on her feet, because she refuses to do anything else.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"There." {n}Her voice is a woman's voice now, hoarse and very tired, and nothing moves in the shadows when she speaks.{/n}
"The cauldron holds a life's worth of the Abyss. Whether it holds a life, we will learn at the rift, and not before." {n}The diamond is cracked along one face; a thread of violet light leaks from the crack and fades.{/n} "It held. It may not hold long enough. If it does not, the rift will take me anyway, and you will have paid for a trinket with the only part of me that did not hurt." {n}She looks at her own hands, and they are shaking, and she lets them.{/n} "It hurts, Commander. I had forgotten that anything could."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"The wager stands, Commander. One of us burns." {n}Areelu does not lower her chin. Blood runs from the wound above her heart, and she does not look at it.{/n}
"Unless you have come to change the terms. You have that look."

Choices.Text: [Raise the stakes] "If neither of us burns, you keep studying me. At close range. For the rest of your thirty years."
[Raise the stakes on your late terms] "Keep your terms. If neither of us burns, you keep studying me, at close range, for the rest of your thirty years."
"At the gate you said you'd thought of little else. Neither had I."
[Ask her to raise them] "Raise them? Here? You'd have to trust me."
[Collect the stake only] "Only the stake. Nothing more."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu

Choices.Text: [Raise the stakes] "If neither of us burns, you keep studying me. At close range. For the rest of your thirty years."
[Ask her to raise them] "Raise them? Here? You'd have to trust me."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Thirty years." {n}She repeats it with clinical interest, as if you had named a dosage.{/n}
"I opened the Wound before your grandparents were born, Commander, and the Abyss runs in my veins. Thirty is not a number I have any use for." {n}Her eyes narrow.{/n} "Unless you know something I do not. You have been knowing things you should not since Kenabres."

Choices.Text: "You told me yourself, at the rift. Years, or decades. I picked a number."
[Joke] "Call it a punchline. You'll get it later."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I said the Wound would kill me in years, or decades." {n}Her voice is flat.{/n} "I did not say which."
"You have chosen a number for me, as if you meant to hold me to it. You are either very foolish or very well informed, and I have not yet decided which frightens me more."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text: "And if I burn, Commander?" {n}Her eyes do not leave your face.{/n} "You have never said what you collect. 'What is left of me' is not a quantity. I will not accept a term I cannot measure."

Choices.Text: "Your notes. A century of them. That's what's left of you."
"We named it in your cell. Your notes."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"My notes." {n}She is silent, and you can watch her test it, the way she tests everything: from the end backwards.{/n}
"Yes. A century of paper. That is exactly what is left of me; everything else went into the Wound." {n}She touches the wound above her heart.{/n} "And the graft that holds the Abyss in me. I made myself, Commander. That was a working too, and a working is work. If you collect my work, you collect the stitch." "Very well. If you collect my work in place of my life, you pay for the privilege. Your wound is mine, win or lose. For study."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"My notes. Yes. You said so in my cell, and I have thought of little else. The notes, and the graft with them: I made myself, and what I made is work." {n}Blood runs from her wound; she does not look at it.{/n}
"Then this is what it costs you, to let paper burn in my place. Your wound is mine, win or lose. For study. You will not get a better term from me, and you will not get this one twice."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"My life, then." {n}She nods, once, as if a sum had come out the way she expected.{/n}
"That is the term the hunters wanted, and the Queen's knights, and the Lady of Graves. You are in good company, Commander. If I burn, I burn, and you collect nothing but ash."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}For a moment she is silent, and you can see her calculate it, as she has calculated everything for a century.{/n}
"You have me beaten, and you are bargaining instead of cutting. At Iz you bet when you could have struck. In my cell you shook hands with a ghost. At the gate you asked about terms." {n}She wipes the blood from her mouth.{/n} "I have stopped calling it weakness. I have no word for it yet. I would like the time to find one."
"If neither of us burns, I spend what is left of me studying you, at close range, until I understand how you did it. And you spend it being studied."
"Understand what you are asking for. I do not run an experiment at arm's length. It will want proximity, of every kind the subject permits, and I will decide where its edges are, not you." {n}A pause.{/n} "The day it stops serving me, I end it, and you will be told the result. Those are the conditions. Very well. I accept."

Choices.Text: [Take her hand. The real one, this time.]

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
{n}Her hand is cold, slick with her own blood, and much stronger than it looks. She grips back hard enough to hurt, and does not let go when a sensible person would.{/n}
"There. The real one, as you asked in my cell." {n}She lets go at last.{/n} "You will find, Commander, that I keep every appointment I make."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"No." {n}She says it without heat.{/n}
"I do not renegotiate at the edge of the Wound, with a sword at my throat. The wager stands as it was struck. Collect your stake, if you win it. Nothing more."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I am afraid of nothing that can be calculated." {n}The blood has reached her wrist. She lets it.{/n}
"You cannot be calculated. That is the whole of my objection, Commander, and it is enough. The answer is no."

Scenes.Title: Nothing to regret
Scenes.Entry: "Regret nothing? Good. You'll want a clear head for the next thirty years."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu

Choices.Text: "Whatever I choose now, the wager stands."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"The wager stands." {n}She says it the way a priest says the end of a prayer: not hoping, only confirming.{/n}
"Whoever burns pays up. I have not forgotten a single clause, Commander, and I will not begin now." {n}She looks past you, at whatever you are about to do.{/n} "Go on. I am watching. I have always been watching."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"I will." {n}She repeats it without inflection, the way she repeats everything she intends to test.{/n}
"Then choose, and let us both find out what you have written. I will not beg, and I will not flinch. Whatever it is, I will want to see it with my eyes open."

Nodes.Speaker: Areelu
Nodes.Text:
"Small print." {n}For a moment, at the very end of everything, the corner of her mouth moves.{/n}
"You have been reading my clauses back to me all day. Very well. Choose, Commander. I will find your small print afterwards, if there is an afterwards. I always find it. That is what I do."

Scenes.ReturnText: {n}Areelu waits for your choice. She regrets nothing.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Nenio
Ember
Nodes.Text:
"You made a bet with the sad lady." {n}Ember twists a strand of her hair around one finger, thinking hard.{/n}
"If she loses, will she be sad? She said she doesn't remember what regret feels like."
"I don't think she forgot it. I think she just forgot where she put it. That happens to me with shoes."
"If you win, will you help her look? I think it would be nice if somebody helped her look."

Nodes.Speaker: Seelah
Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}The report on the experiment called Areelu Vorlesh should have ended at Threshold, where it began: with the siphon bursting, and its sparks dragging her to the edge of the rift, and her life spent to open the new rifts, exactly as the Commander's joke required.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Joke] "Welcome to being mortal. The food's better than you'd think."

Paragraphs.Text: Fine. Then how about this: what the sparks dragged into the rift was the Abyss, and not the woman. An hour before, the Commander had collected her stake into the Council's soul cauldron, a vessel made to drink the essence of another plane, and the essence of another plane was what she had sewn into herself a century ago. When the siphon burst, the rift took what was in it: a quantity, as her first hypothesis said. It did not come back for the woman. Her second hypothesis was wrong, and she wrote so in the margin, twice.

The laboratories of Threshold burned in the same fire: a century of notes, the soul research, the Nahyndrian ledgers, every page she had written in that prison. She watched them go from the edge of the rift and did not try to save one. They had been part of the stake too.

It cost the Commander the wound. That had been her price at Threshold for letting the cauldron take the Abyss in her place: win or lose, the Commander's wound was hers to keep, for study. She collected it the same night, with a silver probe, and it never closed again for anyone but her.

It cost her the stake she had put on the table herself. The Commander had come late to the wager, and had agreed to worse terms: whatever burned, the Commander was to keep nothing of hers. The Commander kept nothing. She kept the rest.

The lens she had left the Commander after Iz cracked straight across in that same moment, in a pack on the floor of Threshold, with a sound like a small bone breaking. Nobody noticed but the Commander.
The woman walked out of the smoke with grey at her temples, no magic at all, and ink on her fingers that would not wash off.
She did not take the hand the Commander held out. She looked at it: the real one, as asked for in her cell. "Not yet," she said. "I am taking an inventory."

She did not look back at Threshold. The Commander did, once, and saw the smoke go up from the place where a century of her work was burning, and understood, too late to say so, that this was the fire the hunters had wanted all along, and that the joke had given it to them, and that she knew.

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She sat down in the ash at the edge of the rift and took it methodically: a word of power, which did nothing; a gesture that had once split stone, which did nothing; her own pulse, counted against the Commander's breathing, which was fast, and hers, and mortal.{/n}
{n}Then she put her face in her hands and made a sound the Commander had never heard from her and never heard again. It was not weeping. It was the noise a door makes when it is forced.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"Mortal." She tried a word of power on the Commander, very deliberately, to see what would happen. Nothing happened. "You took a century from me with a crystal and a pun, and you are recommending the food."{/n}
{n}Her hands were shaking. She held them up between them and looked at them, and let the Commander see her look.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}When she stood up, her face was composed again, and colder than the Commander had ever seen it.{/n}
{n}"Here is what I will do," said Areelu Vorlesh. "I will follow you until I understand how you did it. Not because I want to. Because I lost, and I do not leave an experiment until I know why it failed. You will not read my notes. You will not pity me. When you cease to interest me, I will go, and I will not say goodbye."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Say nothing. Hold out your hand again.]

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She looked at the hand for a long time. Then she took it, briefly, the way one takes a document one intends to read later, and let it go.{/n}
{n}"Noted," she said.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator

Paragraphs.Text: A kitsune scholar arrived within the week, with calipers and a folio, to measure her. Areelu allowed it exactly once, and corrected the arithmetic.

The first inquisitors who came looking for the Architect of the Worldwound found a tired woman with ink on her hands and no magic about her at all, and went away again. She watched them go from an upstairs window, and wrote down how long it took them to stop looking back.

She did not sleep the first night. She sat by the window of the Commander's lodging with a borrowed pen and wrote, from memory, the first page of the report she had been writing all her life, the one the Commander's joke had burned. Then she tore it up. "Wrong," she said. "All of it. I shall have to start again. You have given me a great deal of work."

The late terms had promised the Commander nothing of hers if she burned. She held the Commander to them with great precision for the rest of her life: the Commander was never once allowed to keep a page she had written, and every note she left on the Commander's pillow was taken back by breakfast.

Among the few things she kept was the entry she had dictated in Alushinyrra, which she had never written down and did not need to: "Further observation required." She wrote it on the first page of the new notebook, and underlined it twice.

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}The wager said that whoever burned at Threshold would pay up. She burned, and the stake was never collected in time.{/n}

Paragraphs.Text: Nobody had ever said what with. An open term is a term the other side fills in, and the other side had always been the same: the hunters of Threshold, the Queen's knights, the Lady of Graves.
Her work had been named as the stake, and nobody called it in. There is no rewriting a debt that was left on the table.
The Commander had taken the Abyss out of her into the cauldron, and then chose another ending for what was left. The choice was the Commander's. The report does not argue with it.
She fell in the fight, before anyone could bargain, as she had always said one of them would.

Among what was found in her cell under Threshold was a notebook with a single page written in it, dated the night of the wager: "Stake not yet collected. One of us will regret it." It did not say which.

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Neither of them burned, which was the bet the Commander had made at Iz: "My money's on neither."{/n}
{n}Areelu Vorlesh paid what she owed on the bet from Iz in person. She burned her own notes in front of the Commander, page by page, without comment, for a whole night. What was left of her she kept, as the raised terms allowed, to spend on learning how the Commander had done it: the Abyss still in her veins, and the wound still glowing above her heart. A week later she came to the Commander's door with a proposal, set out as she would have put it to a patron funding a study: rooms across the hall, unrestricted access to the subject, and the right to leave without notice. The Commander set one condition of their own, that she knock. She took an hour to consider it, and accepted, and moved in that evening with a fresh notebook.{/n}

Paragraphs.Text: She objected, on principle, to the fact that the winner was now partly Shyka the Many, and required every observation to be initialled twice: once for each of them.
Nenio offered to buy the ashes for her encyclopaedia. Areelu sold them to her at a price that made the kitsune's ears go flat.
She kept every appointment she made. The first was at the Commander's door, the morning after Threshold, with her hand held out: the real one.

Some of the pages she burned the Commander recognised. The notes from Kenabres. The observations from Drezen, in Yaniel's borrowed hand. A thick bundle tied with black ribbon, labelled only with the Commander's name and a date from before the Commander was born. She burned that one last, and slowest, and watched it until the ribbon was ash.
The lens from Iz she did not burn. She took it back without asking, polished it on her sleeve, and set it on the windowsill between the two rooms, where it stayed.

The Commander, as the report records with some irritation, fell asleep in a chair before she was halfway through, and she burned the rest by the light of the Commander's snoring. "The subject," she wrote, "does not know how to watch a thing end. That is either why it won, or how."

Scenes.Title: The report: the rooms across the hall

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}The report resumed in a clean notebook, bought with the Commander's money from a stationer who did not recognise his customer. First entry: "Subject and observer now live on opposite sides of one hallway. Door left open. Neither party admits to having left it open."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Slide a note under her door instead.]

Paragraphs.Text: She had no magic left to ward her door with, and did not pretend otherwise. Every night she wedged a chair under the handle. Every morning she moved it back before the Commander could see, and every morning the Commander saw.

She did not rely on the chair. Within the week she had three false names registered in three cities, a forger in Nerosyan who owed her a favour from before the crusade, and a standing arrangement with a chandler to warn her of anyone asking after a grey-haired Sarkorian woman. None of it was the Commander's doing, and she made sure the Commander knew that.
She warded her door with three sigils that the Commander could not read, and one that the Commander could. It said, in plain Common: Knock.

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"Enter." She did not look up from the notebook. "You knocked. A subject who knocks is being polite, and politeness is noise. Sit where the light falls on you."{/n}
{n}She measured the Commander's pulse with two cold fingers and a sand-glass, the old wound from Kenabres with a silver probe she had bought from a barber, and the Commander's patience with silence. Of the three, she seemed to find the silence the most interesting.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The sigils flared at the first knock and went out at the second. "Enter," she said, and the door opened by itself, which she clearly thought was funnier than the Commander did.{/n}
{n}She did not need instruments. She laid two fingers against the Commander's wrist and one against the old wound from Kenabres, closed her eyes, and listened, the way she had once listened to the Worldwound. "Your blood is louder than it should be," she said. "Your soul is quieter. Sit down. This will take all night."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She was standing at the window with a glass vial held up to the light, and did not turn around.{/n}
{n}"You did not knock. Good. Subjects who walk in are informative." She set the vial down. It held a single drop of the Commander's blood, taken, she explained, while the Commander slept, because a sleeping subject does not flinch, and a flinch spoils the sample. "You may be angry. Write it down first. I want to know how long it takes."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The sigils hissed like a kettle as the Commander stepped through them, and did nothing else. She had keyed them, it turned out, to everyone in Golarion but one.{/n}
{n}"You did not knock," said Areelu, from the far side of a table covered in the Commander's own hair, nail parings and old bandages, labelled and pinned. "Good. I wanted to see whether you would. It is in the file now. Everything you do is in the file. Do not touch that; it is your left thumb."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Of everything about the Commander, she was most interested in the hands. She drew them from six angles, measured the span from thumb to smallest finger, and asked for the same gesture a hundred times: the small flourish a conjurer makes before a coin disappears.{/n}
{n}"This," she said at last, touching one knuckle with the tip of her pen. "This is where it happens. Not in the soul. In the hands. You decide on the joke before you know it is a joke."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Take the pen out of her hand.]
"And where does it happen in you?"

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander tried. A joke about the Worldwound, which she corrected. A joke about Deskari, which she improved. A face, which she recorded. Then, at last, out of nowhere, a very old and very stupid joke about a paladin, a demon and a goat, which had no business working on anyone.{/n}
{n}She did not laugh. She put her pen down, very carefully, and pressed the back of her wrist against her mouth, and her shoulders shook for almost a minute. "That," she said, when she could, "is inadmissible. It proves nothing. Do it again tomorrow, under controlled conditions."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"In the eyes." She did not hesitate; she had clearly asked herself the same question and answered it long ago. "I see the result before anyone else does. That is all genius is, Commander: seeing the end of the sum while other people are still carrying the one."{/n}
{n}She turned her pen over in her fingers. "It is also why I have never once been surprised by a joke. Until recently." She did not say when. She wrote it down.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}Entry, the end of the first month, last line: "Subject laughs when frightened. Observer does not. Correction pending."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}In the second season, the hunters came.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Joke] "Leave this to me. I have a scarecrow and a spare robe."

Paragraphs.Text: They came from Mendev with a writ and a fire-blessed brand, looking for the Architect of the Worldwound. What they found at the Commander's door was a greying woman with ink on her hands, who did not look to them like anyone in particular.

They came from Mendev with a writ and a fire-blessed brand, and they knew exactly whom they were looking for. The Architect of the Worldwound had been seen alive after Threshold, and there were men in Mendev who had waited all their lives for the chance.

Areelu watched them from the window, and, alone of all the days the Commander had known her, she did not write anything down. The last time witch-hunters had come to her door, she had been at her desk, recording her observations, and her child had been outside.

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The hunters found the Architect of the Worldwound three days later, in a burnt-out farmhouse on the Sarkorian border: a straw witch in a scorched red robe, with a note pinned to her chest in the Commander's handwriting.{/n}
{n}Nobody in Mendev ever repeated what the note said. They burned the straw witch anyway, because they had come a long way.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Areelu read of the burning in a Mendevian broadsheet and laughed until she had to sit down. It was the first time the Commander had heard her laugh as though she meant it. It did not last.{/n}
{n}"They burned a doll and went home satisfied. That is all they ever wanted, Commander. Not the witch. The fire." She folded the broadsheet very small and put it inside her notebook. "I will keep this. It is the most accurate thing anyone in Mendev has ever written about me."{/n}

Choices.Text: "Do you want to know what the note said?"

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"No." She did not look up from the broadsheet. "I know what it said. It said the same thing you said to me at Iz."{/n}
{n}"Neither," said Areelu Vorlesh, and for a moment she sounded almost fond. "You pinned it to a straw woman and let Mendev burn it. That is the most romantic thing anyone has ever done in my presence, and it happened three days' ride away, to a doll. I suppose that is the only way it could have happened."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She went down to them herself, in a plain grey dress, with her hands open to show there was nothing in them.{/n}
{n}"I knew the woman you want," Areelu told the inquisitor. "She was cleverer than you, and crueller, and she did everything you say she did, and more. She is gone. What is left of her would not burn to your satisfaction. There is nothing in it." He believed her, because every word was true.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She came back upstairs with her face very still.{/n}
{n}"Every word of it was true," she said. "That is the trick of it. You taught me that, Commander: tell them the truth in an order they do not expect." Her hands were shaking. She looked at them with the same detached interest she gave everything else, and wrote down how long it took them to stop.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander stood in the doorway beside her, with nothing in either hand, and let the inquisitors look.{/n}
{n}"You will want to arrest the Commander of the crusade as well, I suppose," said Areelu, pleasantly, from behind the Commander's shoulder. "Do. I should like to watch you try." They did not try. They looked from the Commander to the grey-haired woman with ink on her hands, and could not make the two halves of the story fit, and went away to argue about it in a tavern.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander stood in the doorway beside her, with nothing in either hand, and let the inquisitors look.{/n}
{n}"You will want to arrest the Commander of the crusade as well, I suppose," said Areelu, pleasantly. "Do. I should like to watch you try." They did not try. The Commander had walked out of Threshold alive, which in Mendev was reckoned the more frightening of the two, and the witch at the Commander's side was smiling in a way that made the fire-blessed brand go out in its holder.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She let herself be hidden. That was the part the Commander never forgot afterwards: the Architect of the Worldwound going down the cellar steps without a word, with her notebook under her arm, and sitting among the apple barrels in the dark while the hunters searched the house above her.{/n}
{n}They did not find her. When the Commander went down to tell her so, she was writing by the light of a single candle, and did not look up.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"The last time they came," she said, "I did not hide. I did not know to. I was at my desk, and I did not hear them until it was over."{/n}
{n}She closed the notebook. "This time I heard every step. I counted them. Forty-one, in the room above, and three on the cellar door, and then they went away." She stood up, and brushed the dust from her skirt. "Do not do that again. I do not like knowing how it would have felt."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}When they had gone, she stayed in the doorway a while longer, looking at the empty street.{/n}
{n}"The last time they came to my house," she said, "nobody stood in the door." She did not say anything else. That night the entry in her notebook was one line long, and the Commander was not allowed to read it.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}Other hunters would come, in other seasons, from Mendev and from further off. She kept a list of them in the back of the notebook, in the order they arrived, with a mark beside the ones she had let go and another beside the one she had kept.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}In the second winter she fell ill.{/n}
{n}It was nothing: a cough, a fever, the kind of thing that goes through a city every winter and kills the old and the unlucky. The woman who had opened the Worldwound had not been ill in a hundred years. She lay in bed with her notebook on her chest and recorded her own temperature every hour, in a hand that got smaller and smaller, until she could not hold the pen.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Joke] "The Architect of the Worldwound, laid low by a cold. Nobody's going to believe this."
"You could let it take you. You always said you wanted to beat death, not dodge it."

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She opened her eyes, and for a moment they were the eyes the Commander remembered from Threshold, entirely without mercy.{/n}
{n}"Let it take me," she repeated. "In a bed, of a cough, a hundred years late, because you made a pun." She laughed, and it turned into coughing. "No. If death wants me it will have to earn me properly. I will not give it the satisfaction of a cold." She lived, the Commander was sure afterwards, mostly out of spite.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"Nobody will," she agreed, from behind a wall of blankets. "That is the most dangerous kind of truth. Write it down for me. My hand is shaking."{/n}
{n}The Commander wrote it down. She dictated the rest of the night's entry through chattering teeth, correcting the Commander's spelling, and once, near dawn, laughed at something the Commander had written that was not meant to be funny, and would not say what.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}In the second winter the Commander woke one night and found her gone.{/n}
{n}She had not paid the Abyss back when she paid her stake. It was still in her, the half of her she had sewn to her own soul at the edge of the Wound a century ago, and it was hungry the way the Abyss is always hungry. Some nights she did not sleep. Some nights she went out.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Go back to sleep. She will come back.]

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander found her at the edge of the city, where the old walls gave out onto open ground, standing perfectly still with her face turned toward the north, toward the Wound. The wound above her heart was burning violet in the dark.{/n}
{n}"Go home," she said, without turning. "This is not a thing you need to see." And then, when the Commander did not go: "It calls. It has always called. I am standing here so that I can hear it and not answer. That is all I do, on these nights. I stand and I do not answer."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Stand beside her, and do not answer either.]
"I have one too. You put it there."
"What does it say, when it calls?"

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"That I was right." Her eyes stayed on the north. "That everything I did was correct, and there is more to do, and I am wasting the Abyss in me on a kitchen and a notebook and a Commander who makes jokes."{/n}
{n}"It is not wrong," she said. "That is what makes it difficult. It has never once lied to me. It simply does not understand why I have stopped listening, and neither, some nights, do I."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Stand beside her, and do not answer either.]

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander stood beside her until the sky went grey. Neither of them said anything. Once, near dawn, the Commander felt the old rage from Kenabres stir, the half of the Commander's own soul that she had put there, and felt her notice it, and felt her hand close very briefly around the Commander's wrist, hard enough to bruise.{/n}
{n}"There," she said. "Now you know. We are the only two in the world who can hear it. It is not a comfort. It is a fact."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"Yes." She turned at last, and her crimson eyes were very bright. "I changed myself by sewing my soul to the Abyss, and then I changed you. The rage you had in Kenabres was the first stitch."{/n}
{n}"So do not look at me as if I were a stranger standing in the dark. I am your maker in this, Commander, and in nothing else, and it is the one thing between us I will not deny. Come here. Listen. And do not answer."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She came back an hour before dawn, with frost in her hair and nothing in her hands. She saw the Commander sitting up in the dark, and stopped in the doorway.{/n}
{n}"You waited," she said. "I did not ask you to." She sat down on the end of the bed and began, methodically, to take the frost out of her hair. "I have not killed anyone. I have not answered it. Write that down. I want it in your hand, not mine."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander went back to sleep, and she came back, and in the morning there was a new entry in her notebook in a hand that was not quite as steady as usual.{/n}
{n}"Went out. Did not answer. Subject slept through it, which is either trust or stupidity. Recording both."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}It happened perhaps twice a year. She never answered. Once, near the end of the report, she wrote: "A hundred years ago I would have gone. The difference is not virtue. The difference is that I now have somewhere to come back to, and I dislike leaving an experiment unattended."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}In the third year a woman came to the house from the refugee camps on the old Sarkorian border. She carried a roll of birch bark as long as she was tall, wound on a staff, and she asked for the Architect by name.{/n}
{n}It was a clan roll: the names of her people, every family of her grandmother's valley, written in the old way by a god-caller who had not lived to finish it. The Wound had swallowed the valley in its first year. The roll ended in the middle of a name.{/n}

Choices.Text: [Send her away before Areelu sees her.]

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator

Choices.Text: [Ask Areelu to read the names aloud.]
[Ask the woman what she came for.]
[Joke] "Just tell her you're sorry. It's a very short speech."

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Areelu read the names aloud. All of them, the whole length of the staff, in a flat, clear voice, without stopping and without apology. It took the whole night.{/n}
{n}When she reached the end, where the god-caller's hand had stopped in the middle of a name, she stopped too. She did not finish it. She did not pretend to know how it ended.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The woman from the camps wound the bark back onto its staff and left without a word. At the door she turned, once, and looked at Areelu the way one looks at weather: something that has happened, and will happen again.{/n}
{n}"She wanted me to weep," Areelu said afterwards. "I read her the names instead. It was the only honest thing I had to give her. Do not look at me as if it were more than that."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}"I came for her name," said the woman from the camps. "The roll is of everyone the valley lost. She is the last thing the valley lost. She was one of us, before."{/n}
{n}Areelu went white, and then very still. It was the only time the Commander ever saw her surprised by a stranger.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She took the roll. She wrote at the bottom of it, under the god-caller's unfinished name, in the old Sarkorian letters she had not used in a hundred years: "Areelu Vorlesh, of Sarkoris. Lost in the first year, by her own hand."{/n}
{n}"Now go," she said, and the woman went. Afterwards Areelu sat at the kitchen table until the candle burned out, and when the Commander came in she said only: "It was correct. I checked it twice."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander said nothing, and so neither did anyone else. The three of them sat in the kitchen with the roll across the table until the candle burned down.{/n}
{n}When the woman from the camps stood to go, Areelu spoke without looking up. "The last name. The one the god-caller did not finish. Do you know how it ends?" The woman did. She told her. Areelu wrote it down, and never read it aloud, and never crossed it out.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The Commander met the woman at the gate and sent her back to the camps with money and a lie.{/n}
{n}Areelu had watched it all from the window. "You protected me from a list," she said. "How sentimental. I opened the Wound, Commander. I do not need to be shielded from its paperwork." For a week afterwards she spoke to the Commander only in measurements.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She never spoke of the clan roll again. But from that year on she wrote her notes in Sarkorian, which she had not done since Threshold.{/n}
{n}Once, much later, the Commander asked her why. She thought about it for a long time. "Because somebody should still be writing in it," she said at last, "and the ones who had the right are in the Wound. It is not an apology. It is a language. I will not let the last person who writes it be a clerk in Mendev."{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text: {n}Entry, the fourth winter: "Subject has asked a question I cannot answer by observation. Proposal: participation."{/n}

Choices.Text: [Take the notebook out from under her arm.]
"Is that what you want? Not what you're measuring. What you want."

Paragraphs.Text: She was mortal now, and cold at night in a way she had forgotten a body could be. She said so, as a fact, standing in the Commander's doorway with her notebook under her arm and her hair down, which the Commander had never seen before.

The wound above her heart glowed faintly in the dark, as it had at Threshold. She stood in the Commander's doorway with her notebook under her arm and her hair down, which the Commander had never seen before, and the light of the wound showed exactly how little else she was wearing.
"Well?" said Areelu Vorlesh. "Are you going to stand there, or are you going to be studied?"

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She studies you the way she has studied everything: thoroughly, without hurry, and without ever deciding whether what she is doing is study or want. She has never once separated the two. Your shirt she undoes one button at a time, each a separate observation, and pushes it off your shoulders with both hands.{/n}
{n}Cold fingers. Every scar gets its question. The old wound from Kenabres she kisses once, very precisely, as if taking a sample; then again, not precisely at all, her mouth open against your skin.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Her own body she offers the same way, as evidence. The grey dress falls. She stands in the lamplight and covers nothing: the grey at her temples, the new lines at her mouth, the plain mortal warmth come back into her skin after a century of the Abyss. "Look," she says. "Everything you did to me. I want you to see all of it."{/n}
{n}You look. Then she pushes you down onto the bed and climbs astride your hips, palms flat on your chest, and bends to your mouth. Somewhere on the floor the notebook falls open, face down, and she does not go looking for it.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}She studies you the way she has studied everything: thoroughly, without hurry, and as if the question of why were one she will get to afterwards. Her hands are fever-hot, not cold. The half of her that belongs to the Abyss runs close under the skin, and you feel it wherever she touches, like the heat off a forge.{/n}
{n}She does not bother with buttons. Your shirt is simply gone, and so is her robe, and the violet light of the wound above her heart runs over bare skin like water.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}The old wound from Kenabres she kisses once, very precisely. The wound above her own heart flares in answer until the room is full of its light. Crimson to the edges of her eyes. "Yes," she says, against your mouth, as if confirming a result, and then she is not confirming anything.{/n}
{n}She pulls you down on top of her, rolls you both, and comes up astride, her hair a curtain around your faces, her hands pinning your wrists to the pillow. The notebook is somewhere on the floor. She does not go looking for it until morning.{/n}

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
{n}Morning, and grey light, and Areelu sitting on the edge of the bed with the notebook on her knee, writing fast.{/n}
{n}"Do not read over my shoulder," she said, without turning. "You will not like the adjectives." The Commander read over her shoulder anyway. The entry was very long and very precise, and in the margin, in a smaller hand, as if someone else had written it: "Observer compromised. Continue observation."{/n}

Paragraphs.Text: Nenio arrived at breakfast that morning with a folio of questions, took one look at the two of them, and wrote something down. Areelu confiscated the page, read it, corrected the spelling, and gave it back.

Nodes.Speaker: Narrator
Narrator
Nodes.Text:
